findings.summary: The 'a MEAN was quoted where the sentence speaks of PREFIXES' diagnosis is refuted by measurement: the old 7.3x WAS a cumulative-prefix minimum, of the superseded profile. Each old comment had ONE error, not two.
findings.detail: REPRODUCED out of tree (no file added to the repository; sequencer test runtime classpath, 1,000 seeds, ROUNDS=120, PODS=3). Under the SUPERSEDED profile (0.05,0.05,0.1,0) -- the table row at line 87 the comment correctly identifies as the source of '74.17 per seed' -- readers are 74.17/seed, the MEAN clearance against a floor of 10 is 7.417x, and the cumulative-prefix MINIMUM is 7.322x at N=94. The old comment said 7.3x. That is the prefix minimum, rounded, not the mean; its sentence ('clears every cumulative prefix by 7.3x') and its number agreed. The same holds by arithmetic alone on the ack side: 17.53/5 = 3.506x, but the old comment said 3.09x, so whatever 3.09 was it was not a mean either, and 3.09 < 3.506 is the signature of a prefix minimum. So the claim standing at lines 302-303 ('"7.3x" was a MEAN where the sentence it sits in speaks of cumulative PREFIXES'), its restatement at lines 323-325 ('Same two errors as the readers floor above'), and backlog.md:78's headline 'TWO ERRORS IN EACH COMMENT, NOT ONE' are all false in their second half. The single error in each old comment was the stale profile. Concrete failure scenario: the next person tightening these floors reads that the predecessor confused means with prefix minima, concludes prefix-derived figures in this file are untrustworthy, and either re-derives what was already right or applies a spurious safety margin. This is the same class of defect M5.30 exists to remove -- a number-about-numbers that cannot be reasoned from -- one level up. It does not touch any assertion, so it is minor. Everything else in both comments reproduces EXACTLY: 85,458 readers (85.46/seed), 160,478 ack events (160.48/seed), mean clearances 8.5458x and 32.0956x, prefix minima 8.2000x and 30.6000x, both at N=1, seed 0 at 82 readers and 153 acks. The 'no interior dip' claim holds too: the minimum prefix ratio over N>=2 is 8.3500x (readers) and 31.1000x (acks), both at N=2, and the deepest interior values are 8.4594x and 32.29x.
findings.failure_scenario: The next person tightening these two floors reads that the predecessor quoted MEANS where the sentence spoke of cumulative PREFIXES, concludes the prefix-derived figures in this file are untrustworthy as a class, and either re-derives 8.20x/30.60x from scratch or adds a spurious safety margin to a floor. MEASURED refutation: the superseded profile (0.05,0.05,0.1,0) gives readers 74.17/seed, mean clearance 7.417x, cumulative-prefix MINIMUM 7.322x at N=94 -- the old comment's 7.3x is the prefix minimum, not the mean. On the ack side, arithmetic alone: 17.53/5 = 3.506x, and the old comment said 3.09x, so 3.09 was not a mean either.

findings.summary: The corrected 30.60x is headroom over a trace that is 93% CONFIRMED events. Blinding the ACK half -- the only half checkAckOrder predicates on -- survives this floor at 29.83x. SURVIVING MUTATION: delete the three acks.add(...acked(...)) calls in CommitProtocolSimulation (lines 406, 570, 597).
findings.detail: MEASURED, 1,000 seeds: of the 160.48 ack events per seed, 149.37 are CONFIRMED (store-sourced, M4.50) and only 11.11 are ACK events -- one per commit. checkAckOrder's only two found.add sites are unreachable for a non-ack event (the loop does `if (!e.isAck()) { ...; continue; }`), so a trace carrying no ACK events reports nothing, forever -- which is verbatim what this assertion's .as string says it exists to refuse. DEMONSTRATED end to end over 200 seeds, out of tree, using M4.50's own falsifiability defect (ack sequence+1): on the full trace checkAckOrder reports 2,295 violations; with the ACK half of the trace stripped it reports 0; and ackEvents under the strip is 29,829 against a floor of 1,000 -- GREEN at 29.83x. The ACK half on its own is 11.11/seed against the floor of 5, a mean clearance of 2.22x, a cumulative-prefix MINIMUM of 1.18x at N=8, and at least one seed emits ZERO ACK events. So the number that guards the quantity at risk is 1.18x, not 30.60x. NOT INTRODUCED HERE -- the floor, its value and its .as string are untouched by this diff, and the 30.60x figure is arithmetically true of ackEvents -- so this does not block, and tightening is a separate task by the packet's own framing. It is recorded because (a) M5.30's stated purpose is that these numbers be reasoned from the next time the floor is tightened, and 30.60x will lead that reader to conclude the ack trace is amply guarded when the ack half is at 1.18x; and (b) backlog.md:37 (M5.28, already committed) cites this floor as the precedent that kills the trace-blinding family -- 'exactly what ackEvents does for the ack trace in the same method' -- and that claim is false for the ack half. Suggested shape if it becomes a row: count and floor the two halves separately (acks().stream().filter(AckEvent::isAck)), noting that a bare per-seed floor on the ack half must respect the 1.18x prefix minimum at N=8 and the zero-ack seed.
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION: delete the three acks.add(AckOrderInvariants.AckEvent.acked(...)) calls in CommitProtocolSimulation.java (lines 406, 570, 597), leaving the store-sourced CONFIRMED half. MEASURED over 200 seeds out of tree, using M4.50's own falsifiability defect (ack sequence+1): checkAckOrder reports 2,295 violations on the full trace and 0 with the ACK half stripped, while ackEvents is 29,829 against a floor of 1,000 -- the floor stays GREEN at 29.83x. I5's ack-ordering clause becomes unfalsifiable and the sweep reports success, which is the exact defect family this floor's own comment says it exists to refuse. The ack half alone is 11.11/seed, mean clearance 2.22x, prefix minimum 1.18x at N=8, with at least one seed emitting zero ACK events.
